_comment: THE VIEWER MUST STILL OFFER AN EQUIP ON A BOARD WIDE ENOUGH TO TRIP THE PLAN-SPACE VALVE. USER, 2026-10-02, playing KittyEquipment v2 in the play viewer: the history filled with '⚠ This board's plan space is too large to enumerate in full (476427292645799936 combinations)' and then -- 'That's actually an incorrect message. I can't equip various equipment.' Both halves were real defects. (1) The printed number was computed by viewerplancap::Estimate as 2^ind x PROD(1+|group|), a rule the engine STOPPED FOLLOWING when MTG_EQUIP_COPY_COLLAPSE went default-ON: the walk only visits positions whose interchangeable-copy digits are non-increasing, so the honest count on a board like this one is ~4,600x smaller than the figure the player was shown. (2) Because the valve then SHRANK against that inflated number, it dropped whole equip groups -- and a dropped group is an action the menu no longer holds, so the line's own promise ('Every action is still reachable one click at a time') was false and the human could not equip at all. This board is the shape that produced it: metalcraft is live (20 artifacts, Puresteel Paladin -> every equip is {0}, so the valve's payable-knapsack refinement filters NOTHING and its estimate degenerates to the raw product), two legal hosts, and five four-of Equipment classes. The fix makes the estimate fold-aware and pools interchangeable duplicates BEFORE dropping any action; this fixture pins the user-visible consequence rather than the internals, so it fails if a future change goes back to deleting equip groups. A bare 'equip=<name>' is the any-source/any-host wildcard, so this asserts only that SOME legal equip of a Kite Shield is enumerated -- which is exactly what the player could not do.
